correctness.rationale: For each ideal vertex a Möbius cusp chart is exactly a vertical strip of width w_i above height H_i; height u=log(y/H_i) has unnormalized density (w_i/H_i)e^-u. For two distinct cusp vertices the exact hyperbolic distance formula yields d=u+v+log(g_ij H_i H_j)+O(e^-u+e^-v); the convolution of two unit exponentials gives (s+1)e^-s. Integrating transition-layer error costs O(e^-R), and arbitrary chart heights cancel. Core/cusp and same-cusp pairs contribute only O(e^-R). Summing both ordered directions and dividing by ((n−2)pi)^2 gives C(P). For vertices (0,1,t,infty), direct substitution C=2t²/[pi²(t−1)], minimized uniquely at t=2. This argument is not a Monte Carlo extrapolation.
residual_risks: The error O_P(e^-R) depends on the fixed polygon; no uniform degeneration estimate.
No finite-vertex or nonconvex extensions are proved.
